title: Frontend: Design Autocomplete
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Design Autocomplete. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({entries,prefix,limit}). Entries have unique lowercase ASCII word and numeric score. Build a prefix index, query case-insensitively, rank matches by descending score then ascending word, return at most nonnegative limit words. Empty prefix matches all. This bounded prefix/ranking core excludes remote personalization.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
For a static prefix dictionary, a trie or sorted-array prefix range can locate candidates.
alternativeApproaches: Compare trie top-k caches with a search index when ranking depends on user context and rapidly changing popularity.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty prefix; no match; equal rank.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
